question.text: For a MIBOR futures contract on a notional principal of Rs. 5 crores with 30/365 day-count convention, using the exact unrounded calculation (without the workbook's Rs. 411-per-bp rounded factor), what is the interest amount for a quoted rate of 7.00% for one month?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the exact unrounded calculation: Notional x Rate x Day-fraction = Rs. 5,00,00,000 x 7.00% x (30/365) = 5,00,00,000 x 0.07 x 0.082192 = Rs. 2,87,671 (option A). This is the precise interest amount required by p.114 of the NISM Series IV workbook. The Trap: Option B (Rs. 2,91,667) uses 30/360 day-count, which is wrong for MIBOR futures. Option C (Rs. 3,50,000) ignores the day fraction. The original ambiguous version had Rs. 2,87,700 as a distractor, which is the value obtained from the workbook's Rs. 411-per-bp shortcut on p.121 (Rate x 100 x 411 = 7.00 x 100 x 411 = Rs. 2,87,700). Because the source contains both methods, both Rs. 2,87,671 and Rs. 2,87,700 were defensible. The Rs. 2,87,700 distractor has been replaced with Rs. 4,11,000 to remove the conflict. Note: The original was ambiguous because the workbook supports both the exact 30/365 calculation (giving Rs. 2,87,671) and a rounded Rs. 411-per-bp shortcut (giving Rs. 2,87,700) for the same inputs. The stem has been tightened to require the exact unrounded calculation, and the Rs. 2,87,700 distractor has been removed. Source: NISM Series IV, Dec 2025, pp.114, 121.
